chunks: Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Khalid, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Do not take (cut) from your hair while you intend the Hajj in Dhu al-Qadah, nor in the month in which you intend to go out for the Umrah.

key_terms.الْحَجَّ: Hajj, the major annual Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca
key_terms.الْعُمْرَةِ: Umrah, the minor Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca
key_terms.تَأْخُذْ: Take/cut, referring to cutting hair or nails in the context of ritual preparation
key_terms.ذِي الْقَعْدَةِ: Dhu al-Qadah, the second of the four sacred months in the Islamic calendar

ai.seo_question: When should a Muslim refrain from cutting their hair before Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies the prohibition of cutting hair for those intending Hajj in Dhu al-Qadah or departing for Umrah, reflecting the preparatory sanctity (*Ihram*-like state) before the formal ritual begins. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on continuous ritual purity and mindfulness from the moment of intention (*Niyyah*), distinguishing it from the strict prohibitions of the actual *Ihram* period. It serves as a practical guideline for pilgrims to maintain physical signs of devotion during the sacred months of Dhu al-Qadah and Dhu al-Hijjah.
